note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient is a 40-year-old woman, four weeks post-cesarean section, presenting with sudden onset of shortness of breath while at rest and a recent cough. Concern raised for possible thromboembolism requiring urgent hospital evaluation.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute Shortness of Breath  
- Sudden onset of shortness of breath for approximately one hour, occurring while at rest (watching TV).  
- Associated with recent onset cough starting one day prior, non-productive.  
- No chest pain reported except soreness with deep inspiration attributed to C-section scar tenderness.  
- No prior episodes of similar symptoms.  
- Palpitations reported with elevated heart rate (~30 beats in 10 seconds, estimated tachycardia).  
- No history of fever or infectious symptoms mentioned.  
- Social history: postpartum status, caring for infant at home; partner currently at work; no mention of smoking or alcohol.  
- Clinical concern raised for pulmonary embolism given recent cesarean section and acute symptoms.  
- Differential includes thromboembolic event versus respiratory infection or other cardiopulmonary causes.  
- Patient advised urgent hospital evaluation; declined ambulance, will self-present.

Issue 2: Recent Cesarean Section  
- Cesarean delivery approximately 4 weeks ago.  
- Use of painkillers including codeine regularly postoperatively, stopped about one week ago.  
- C-section scar tenderness noted on deep inspiration.  
- No complications or other issues reported postoperatively.

Issue 3: Allergy to Ibuprofen  
- Patient reports allergy to ibuprofen; reaction details not documented.  
- Avoidance noted.

Medications:
- Codeine, dose/route/frequency not documented (used post-C-section for pain, ceased about one week ago).

Allergies:
- Ibuprofen (reaction details unknown).

Past Medical History:
- No other medical problems reported.

Social History:
- Lives with partner and newborn infant.  
- Partner currently at work.  
- No smoking or alcohol use documented.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Heart rate estimated at approximately 180 bpm by patient palpation (30 beats in 10 seconds).  
- Chest and C-section scar tenderness on deep inspiration reported by patient.  
- No vitals formally recorded by clinician.

Plan:
- Patient advised immediate hospital assessment for possible pulmonary embolism given recent C-section and acute shortness of breath/palpitations.  
- Patient to avoid taking codeine prior to hospital visit.  
- Patient will self-present to hospital with infant.  
- No ambulance called per patient preference.  
- Further management dependent on hospital evaluation results.
